passage:
A farmer kept a weather diary for forty years. He wrote down rain, wind, planting dates, and harvest results.
His granddaughter used the diary for a school project. She compared older entries with recent years and noticed changes in heat and rain patterns.
The diary was not a scientific station, but it was valuable local evidence.
Her teacher said long-term observation is powerful. Careful notes can become data when kept consistently.
The granddaughter saw her grandfather differently after that. He had not only grown crops. He had recorded a changing world, one day at a time.
